nodes.label: Cost Viability
nodes.why_it_exists: This front exists to stop technically interesting prototype motion from silently becoming an economically weak product story.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Prototype-learning may continue, but product-path narration is capped while economics are mismatched.

nodes.label: Review Fronts
nodes.why_it_exists: This front keeps live bounded decisions and human-review questions visible instead of letting them dissolve into background context.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: These are bounded review fronts only, not approved product commitments.
nodes.summary: V1 Confidence Display Format is the active review front. Operator review is needed on V1 Confidence Display Format.

nodes.label: Implementation Package Review
nodes.why_it_exists: This front keeps one milestone operationally current so ELI does not drift across multiple meaningful fronts at once.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Treat Implementation Package Review only as a prototype-learning and buildability gate. It does not justify discreet consumer product narration while cost posture still says `stop_if_cost_target_matters`.
nodes.summary: Implementation Package Review is the least premature current front because it can still unlock downstream progress without pretending stronger product-facing milestones are ready.

nodes.label: Subsystem Fronts
nodes.why_it_exists: This front keeps the main subsystem pressures legible so downstream realization and review do not over-read thin grounding.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Subsystem gaps are still prototype-limiting and product-capping, especially around wireless, firmware, and memory trust.
nodes.summary: Wireless Interface, Firmware, Memory System currently block stronger downstream confidence.

nodes.label: Parts Readiness
nodes.why_it_exists: This front answers whether ELI can honestly suggest package placeholders, provisional parts, or a stronger shortlist yet.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Package-level posture is valid for prototype planning; it is not a component-shortlist or procurement claim.
nodes.summary: Package-level suggestions are warranted now, but no grounded component-shortlist or equivalent implementation artifact justifies stronger part claims yet.

nodes.label: Pricing & Alternatives
nodes.why_it_exists: This front compares current package directions against cheaper or simpler alternatives without pretending there is vendor-grade pricing certainty.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Pricing direction is still prototype-oriented and does not rescue the current target tier story.
nodes.summary: Current suggestions are still useful mainly for prototype learning. No current or cheaper/simpler alternative is good enough yet for the declared target tier, so stay prototype-only unless cost posture improves.

nodes.label: Build & Realization
nodes.why_it_exists: This front keeps build-oriented structure honest without implying a final implementation package or final BOM.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Build posture is prototype-only, early-subsystem-BOM-only, and explicitly not a consumer-tier implementation package.
nodes.summary: A concrete part list is still premature, but a bounded subsystem-level BOM frame is now warranted to improve buildability and package thinking without pretending the parts are settled.

nodes.label: Exploratory Rendering
nodes.why_it_exists: This front exists only for bounded visual drafting support around packaging, placement, and comparison; it is not design truth.
nodes.prototype_vs_product_posture: Exploratory rendering is subordinate review context only and must not be read as accepted design or solved productness.
